top_signals.title: AI Jitters Haven't Slowed the Bet on U.S. Power Demand
top_signals.summary: We finally have hard data to show us exactly how much energy data centers are using in the United States, and the results are staggering. Driven by the artificial intelligence boom, energy-hungry data centers are popping up in record numbers around the country and driving up domestic energy demand after decades of plateaued growth. Data center hyperscalers in the United States alone now rival the energy demand of entire other nations, with worrying implications for energy security, economic inflation, and the climate. But AI development is careening…
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: Is China Misreading the Moment?
top_signals.summary: When U.S. President Donald Trump lands in Shenzhen later this week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, he will sit down with Chinese leader Xi Jinping for the fourth time amid an unexpected détente between Washington and Beijing. The trade war of 2025 is in abeyance, the two governments have announced a relationship of “constructive strategic stability,” and, to the alarm of American allies, Trump and Xi are planning to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Beneath the surface, however, the détente is beginning to crack.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: CFOs Face Rising Costs, Reluctant Consumers
top_signals.summary: CFOs started the year thinking the fight against inflation was behind them. Heading into the final stretch of 2026 – and the holiday season that’s key for many businesses – it’s clear that it isn’t. Nina Trentmann explains (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: Anthropic IPO: What to Know About the Share Price and Trading Debut
top_signals.summary: In late 2020, a group of senior OpenAI employees unhappy with what they saw as the company’s failure to adequately prioritize AI ethics and safety left the firm to form Anthropic PBC. Just a few years later, the younger company has become an artificial intelligence behemoth that completed the largest initial public offering in history.
